title: E-beam irradiated poly(vinyl-alcohol)/xyloglucan/κ-carrageenan/ovalbumin hydrogels as antioxidant wound dressings
content: Hydrogel wound dressings are interesting medical devices for the management of chronic wounds, owing to their ability to combine fluid uptake, mechanical integrity, conformability and cytocompatibility, while ideally providing biological activity. Chronic wounds arise from disruption of the normal healing cascade, characterized by persistent inflammation, impaired tissue regeneration, and increased susceptibility to infection. In this study, radiation-crosslinkable and sterilized hydrogel formulations were developed by synergistically combining a biocompatible synthetic polymer, poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), with two natural polysaccharides, xyloglucan (XG) and κ-carrageenan (κC), and hen egg white ovalbumin (OVA), with the aim of producing multicomponent hydrogel wound dressings that, beyond the typical properties of hydrogel-based dressings, are processable before irradiation but form a permanent, sterilizable network after irradiation, and can help modulate oxidative stress at the wound site and enhance the healing process. OVA incorporation preserved network formation and cytocompatibility while increasing hydrogel deformability and water uptake. All irradiated formulations showed approximately 100% fibroblast viability, supported fibroblast-mediated scratch closure, and reduced TBH-induced intracellular oxidative stress. Overall, the results demonstrate that e-beam processing enables simultaneous network formation and sterilization, while formulation and FT treatment provide complementary control over the hydration – mechanical balance of the resulting wound dressings.
